newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude near lows on refined product losses.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude near lows on refined product losses.

text.p: NYMEX crude hovered near its session low Friday afternoon, testing technical support, as traders rolled positions out of the expiring prompt refined product contract, sending heating oil to an eight-month low.
"There seems to be a lot of bearish crude guys. Although there are some big players selling right now, I don't think we will break $20.50," said a New York crude trader.
At 1341 EST, April crude was off 29 cents a barrel at $20.60, hitting a session low of $20.52 Friday afternoon, the lowest level for prompt crude since August 1.

"There was a surprisingly high amount of open interest in the March contracts. There was just a lot of speculative length," said a dealer, noting the active rolling of long positions from March to April in gasoline and heating oil.
March heating oil was off 1.28 cents at 54.75 cents after falling to 54.05 cents, spot heat's lowest level since July 1.
March gasoline was off 1.27 cents at 61.60 cents a gallon.

There had been concern earlier in the session of oversupply in gasoline due to cargoes from Europe heading to the New York Harbor, but some traders said they saw nothing extraordinary about the amount of supply expected.
"If there were oversupply it would have shown up in the spreads, but the spreads are firm. The (gasoline) crack is at $5.85 and it closed yesterday at $5.87," said a dealer.

Meanwhile, traders said crude was buffered somewhat from new short positions as local players would not want to leave for the weekend exposed to upside risk. In fact, traders said there may be a short-covering bounce late session.
"We could rally to around $20.80 (in crude) toward the end, so guys are squared by the weekend," said a New York crude dealer.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
